source: Front panel measured 2026-11-24 from polynominal.com's straight-on cut-out of the whole front (private/bsrack/docs/web/polynominal-rack-front.jpg, 4061x1244, SHA1 e539fb19dd789cf12a2dcefa067822f279b3d560). Plate 178..3905 x 441..780 px taken as 482.6 x 44.0 mm (7.72 px/mm on average); the photo's lens distortion (up to 6 % smaller scale at the left end) taken out with a model fitted to the printed frame lines and the knob tick circles, see docs/panel.md. About +-0.2 mm for printed parts; raised parts (caps, keys, levers) as seen.
units: mm from the plate's top left corner; text x/y = anchor (per align) and cap-height centre; angles clockwise from 12 o'clock
colours_note: Median of real pixels, areas in docs/panel.md. The photo is lit from the upper right and warm; the face reads #2d2c26 at the far left. No LED is lit in the photo, so no 'on' colours were measured.

slots.note: The site hand-masked the four slots white, so their outlines are approximate (+-0.4 mm). w/h are the mean of the three clean ones; the lower right one sits under the watermark. Centres 31.7 mm apart vertically (EIA 31.75).

logos.label: Novation logo
logos.note: White 'novation' letters with the small square at their left, at the top of the display window.

logos.label: BassStation Rack logo
logos.note: Blue italic 'BassStation' measured whole. The yellow script 'Rack' is crossed by the site's watermark: the box is the extent of its visible strokes (R swash at the left, top of the k at the right); the strokes under the watermark are assumed to lie inside it.

logos.label: Novation logo (rear)
logos.note: Black: the small square with its emblem, then 'novation' in heavy lower case; the t and i reach the box's top.

logos.label: BassStation Rack logo (rear)
logos.note: Black: 'BassStation' in a serif italic and 'Rack' in a script, as the front's but larger.

frames_note: Boxes run through the centres of the thin light lines; neighbouring frames are separate lines 0.9-1.5 mm apart.
strips_note: Grey legend strip under each knob row, across the full frame width (to the outer edge of the frame lines). The data entry section has none.

titles.note: the slash runs 0.45 mm below the baseline

titles_note: Bold blue capitals on the face just under the strip, not centred on their frames (as printed).
knob_note: Centres from the tick circles (printed, so free of parallax); all 18 on y 14.0 and a 20.0 mm pitch within a section. Caps (blue) and skirts (black, knurled) are tall: in the photo the caps sit up to 4 mm off their shafts at the ends. cap_d 8.9 is the cap top as seen (about 2 % magnified, being nearer the camera); skirt_d 12.6 is the skirt's outline on the knobs nearest the camera axis (230-310 mm). Ticks: 11 white marks 28.2 deg apart over -141..+141 deg, r 6.45-7.98, 0.3 wide. Pointer: white bar on the cap from the centre to the rim.

knobs.name: MIX
knobs.note: MIX has its own scale: an arc (ring) round the skirt from -143 to +141 deg with the ticks standing out from it; the arc is yellow from the EXT. end (-143) to the third tick (-58), light grey after. EXT. is printed yellow. Ring and ticks fitted in mm; centre (190.03, 13.88).

legends.note: bare minus sign, its bar 202.06-203.20 x 20.70-21.08; cap taken from the digit legends

switches_note: Slide switches: a black slot (body) with a ribbed dark grey lever. body x measured per switch (half-level edges); y 28.33..32.95 is common (the top edge is crisp at 28.25-28.38; the bottom edge is a soft shadow, 32.9-33.5, taken from the five cleanest). Lever 5.5 x 3.5 mm (mean of ten), its face seen 29.15..32.65, 0.25 mm low from parallax. lever_x = lever centre for each position, ends 0.8 mm in from the slot ends (the gap measured at end-position levers, 0.6-1.2 mm). photo_at = index of the position the lever sits at in the photo; every lever in the photo sits within 0.5 mm of one of these.

labels.note: AUDITION/DEMO printed as one line: AUDITION white, /DEMO yellow

keys_note: Grey keys, outline at the 25 % level between face and key (includes the darker right and lower side faces the camera sees; the lit face alone is about 9.45 x 4.45). Keypad columns 13.0 mm apart (x 67.3/80.3/93.3), rows 8.5 mm apart. Numerals (white, cap 1.7) sit about 0.9 mm left of the outline centre: the key tops are raised and seen from the right. Yellow second-function labels are printed under their keys; SAVE TYPE and SAVE are printed grey-beige with COMPARE and WRITE in light boxes below them. The MODE key's bracket line runs up towards the SAVE LED.

display.window_note: black bezel with rounded corners; its edges are faint in the photo (+-0.3 mm)
display.digits_note: GUESSED, not measured: the 7-segment digits are unlit and invisible behind the red filter. Boxes assume a 0.4 in (10.16 mm) digit, centred in the filter vertically, with its decimal point at the EDIT/WRITE marks (x 112.54 and 122.55, 10.0 mm apart).
display.led_note: round, behind the window, pale pink (unlit, with a reflection); d at half contrast
display.marks_note: EDIT and WRITE are the two decimal points; each word has a small white corner mark pointing up at its DP. Line 0.25 wide.

leds_note: Red domes, unlit in the photo; d at half chroma contrast (the lens is likely a 3 mm LED, its rim lost in shadow).

phones.note: 1/4 in jack: silver nut ring and black hole; centre between the nut and hole fits (they differ by 0.3 mm from parallax).

name_strip.note: Light strip under the logo with black capitals. The watermark covers the H and the I of SYNTHESIZER and the M of MODULE; the text's right end (463.70) is at the watermark's edge, so its width is +-0.3 mm. Spelling (with a Z) from the same strip on the rear (docs/web/polynominal-rack-rear.jpg); the front's visible Z agrees.

data_entry.note: AUDITION/DEMO printed as one line: AUDITION white, /DEMO yellow

osc2.note: bare minus sign, its bar 202.06-203.20 x 20.70-21.08; cap taken from the digit legends

mod_sync.note: the slash runs 0.45 mm below the baseline

texts_note: Every printed word, by frame. x is the left edge, centre or right edge per align; y is the middle of the capitals; cap is the capital height from the word's bounding box (a few switch legends whose box was 0.1-0.15 taller from round O/G/S overshoot are given their line's flat height; PROTECT/ENABLE the mean of the pair). The same entries appear inside knobs/switches/keys/display above; this list is the complete set.

rear.source: Rear measured 2026-11-25 from polynominal.com's straight-on image of the whole rear (private/bsrack/docs/web/polynominal-rack-rear.jpg, 1032x104, SHA1 df3089582ef130a50539af45e67b71bdd2b649f2). Scale 2.339 px/mm from the jacks' 20.0 mm pitch (CV IN to GATE OUT, the MIDI sockets alike), which makes the plate 1029 px = 440.0 mm, the standard 1U body between the ears; 101 px = 43.2 mm of its height shows. +-0.4 mm for print, +-0.5 mm for the sockets.
rear.frame: the rear plate's millimetres, x from its left edge as seen from behind, y down from its top; the view centres it in the front's 482.6 x 44.0 mm

jacks.name: CV IN
jacks.tip: CV IN: not emulated (the firmware reads it; the plugin has no jack for it)

jacks.name: CV OUT
jacks.tip: CV OUT: not emulated (the firmware sets it: the last MIDI note, 1 V/octave)

jacks.name: OUTPUT: LINE OUT
jacks.tip: OUTPUT: LINE OUT, the plugin's output

jacks.name: MIDI OUT
jacks.tip: MIDI OUT: the plugin's MIDI output (a knob sends its controller)

jacks.name: MIDI THRU
jacks.tip: MIDI THRU: not emulated (it copies MIDI IN)

jacks.name: POWER IN 9V DC
jacks.tip: POWER IN 9V DC: the plugin is the power supply

din.note: 5-pin 180 degree DIN: pins on the lower half, the key notch at the top

texts.text: This device complies with Part 15 of the FCC Rules.
Operation is subject to the following two conditions :
1. This device may not cause harmful interference.
2. This device must accept any interference received,
including interference that may cause undesired operation.

rear.texts_note: Measured from the image's ink: each line's cap centre and width. The FCC lines run together at that resolution: their pitch (2.5 mm, then 2.1 mm) and the block's width (71.4 mm, line 5) are measured, the other lines' widths read off it.
